_doc: Config for managed/scripts/guard-destructive.py, the PreToolUse hook that
hard-denies unrecoverable actions in every security posture.
Copy this to <workspace>/ops/guard-destructive.json and edit it. The
defaults baked into the script are a guess at a workspace layout, and a
protected list that does not match your directories protects nothing.
The guard looks for config in this order:
1. $GUARD_DESTRUCTIVE_CONFIG
2. <workspace>/ops/guard-destructive.json
3. its built-in defaults
<workspace> is $OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE, or ~/clawd. Keys starting with an
underscore are ignored, so this comment block travels with the file.
FIELDS
workspace       absolute path, or omit to use $OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE / ~/clawd
protectedDirs   top-level directories where deletion must be recoverable.
Anything hand-made, generated once, or not reproducible by
rerunning a build belongs here.
ephemeralDirs   directories where `rm` stays allowed, matched at any depth.
Build output, caches, logs, dependency trees. Keep this
honest or you will break your own builds.
recoverableDelete  the command the agent is told to use instead. macOS ships
`trash`. On Linux use "gio trash" or "trash-put".
logPath         relative to the workspace, or absolute.
denyGitDiscard  deny `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, `git checkout --`.
On by default; these discard uncommitted work silently.
denyPrismaMigrateDeploy  off by default, because `prisma migrate deploy` is
the correct production step for a repo that HAS a migration
history. Turn it on only if your production schema is
push-managed, where a deploy replays migrations that were
never applied.
